name: Vacuum Cleaner
blurb: Corded vacuums draw 500–1,400 watts, so a thorough half-hour clean uses under half a kilowatt-hour. Weekly vacuuming across a whole year costs about what one hour of central AC does.

name: Robot Vacuum
blurb: Robot vacuums sip power — a full charge holds 40–80 watt-hours — and their docks idle at a couple of watts. Even daily runs total well under a dollar a month; the convenience costs essentially nothing to operate.

name: Air Purifier
blurb: HEPA purifiers draw 20–60 watts on medium and run around the clock during allergy or smoke season, making runtime the whole cost story. An Energy Star model on auto mode typically costs a couple of dollars a month.
tips: Auto mode with an air-quality sensor cuts runtime dramatically versus always-on high.
Replace filters on schedule — a loaded filter forces higher fan speeds for the same clean air.
Size the purifier to the room; an oversized unit on low beats a small one screaming on high.

name: Treadmill
blurb: Treadmills draw 300–900 watts depending on speed, incline, and runner weight. A 45-minute run uses about half a kilowatt-hour — a month of consistent training costs less than a single studio class.

name: Elliptical
blurb: Ellipticals mostly power a console and resistance system — many are self-powered by pedaling. Plugged-in models draw 50–200 watts, a fraction of a treadmill's motor.

name: Exercise Bike (Smart Trainer)
blurb: Smart bikes and trainers draw 30–100 watts, primarily for the screen. Ride every day and the electricity still rounds to under a dollar a month — the subscription is the real recurring cost.

name: Home Sauna
blurb: Traditional electric sauna heaters draw 3–9 kW and need 30–45 minutes of preheat before sessions, so each sauna evening uses 5–8 kWh. Infrared saunas cut that roughly in half by heating bodies rather than a room of hot rocks.

name: Sewing Machine
blurb: Sewing machines draw about 100 watts including the light. Even a serious quilting habit costs pennies per month — the fabric stash is the budget item.

name: Smart Thermostat
blurb: The thermostat itself draws about a watt — irrelevant. Its value runs the other direction: schedule-driven setbacks typically trim 5–10% from heating and cooling, making it one of the few devices with a negative effective cost.

name: Home Alarm System
blurb: Alarm panels, sensors, and sirens idle at 5–20 watts continuously. That's a dollar or two a month — monitoring fees cost ten times the electricity.

name: Essential Oil Diffuser
blurb: Ultrasonic diffusers draw 5–20 watts. Running one every evening all month costs a few cents; the oils cost hundreds of times more than the electricity.

name: Reptile Heat Lamp / Terrarium
blurb: Reptile setups combine heat lamps, ceramic emitters, UVB tubes, and mats running half the day or more — commonly 50–250 watts in aggregate. A large terrarium can quietly cost more per month than the family refrigerator.

name: Waterbed Heater
blurb: Waterbed heaters keep hundreds of pounds of water at body temperature, historically adding 60–120 kWh a month. Good insulation — pads below, comforter above — is the difference between modest and memorable.

name: Power Tool Battery Charger
blurb: Charging a typical 4–5 Ah tool battery uses under a tenth of a kilowatt-hour. An entire fleet of drill and saw batteries costs less per year than leaving one porch light on for a week.
